brief.scope: Measure launcher feasibility before adapter implementation. Read current AGENTS.md, ops/README.md, accepted startup/harness/permission/probe contracts and supplied adoption review. Investigate installed Claude/Codex/Grok executable/version/help and local non-secret documentation/code first. Determine each actual pre-tool interception or equivalent enforcement mechanism, complete tool coverage including shell and MCP, unattended refusal, configuration injection, actual MCP connection evidence and resume binding. Distinguish observed installed support from assumptions, prompt-only compliance and unavailable measurements. No model launches, network, credentials, global config changes, writes or admission. Report a compact per-harness capability matrix, exact commands/refs/versions, gaps and the smallest contract-preserving path to usable conduct. If a required mechanism is unavailable, say so now; do not prescribe a refusal-only launcher as usable. Inline report only; no PLAN.md.

findings.claim: Launcher-feasibility blocker: installed Grok 1.0.13 cannot satisfy the required failure-closed decision transport through either documented file hooks or SDK hooks alone. The contract requires a 'missing, late, malformed, duplicate or mismatched response' to fail closed. Embedded file-hook documentation says timeouts, crashes and malformed output fail open. Embedded SDK diagnostics explicitly say 'malformed x.ai/hooks/run response; failing open', 'transport error (no client wired?); failing open' and 'timed out; failing open'. Catching exceptions inside a hook cannot cover failure to start or deliver that hook. A separate verified enforcement mechanism is required before implementing Grok as a usable conduct adapter. This is an installed-mechanism incompatibility, not a demonstrated exploit introduced by the diff.

envelope.note:
Feasibility verdict: no harness currently has enough measured evidence to qualify as usable conduct. Grok's hook-only route has a concrete documented incompatibility; Claude and Codex have candidate mechanisms whose complete coverage and failure behavior remain unresolved. This review completed the permitted local measurements; it does not certify the discovery implementation or runtime admission.

Scope and evidence
Read the supplied adoption-review JSON whole, current instructions, founding contracts, ops/README.md, startup/harness/permission/probe contracts, C1/C2 and lane-policy requirements. Base: 710dbac38c3b187eb4b3302308430c0a6dec4d76. In-memory comparison confirmed the supplied 287916-byte patch equals git diff BASE HEAD. git diff --check exited 0. The diff adds discovery/3 implementation and launch-interface contracts; the supplied earlier review's claim that lane_refs.py is absent is superseded. Dispatch/task/harness implementation and .claude/settings.json are unchanged between these refs. Final Git status was empty.

Containment and output gaps
Grok now advertises OS sandboxing, superseding any inference that this installed version has none. Its embedded sandbox guide says ordinary built-in setup failures can continue unenforced; explicit custom profiles have stricter startup refusal, with additional protected-hook-path requirements. Custom read_write entries are documented as directory grants; built-ins also retain runtime/temp writes. None establishes C2's exact leaf/scratch/transport equality. Codex exposes richer filesystem permission types as well as legacy sandbox flags, and Claude exposes sandbox controls; their exact C2 behavior remains unmeasured. Kernel measured by uname -srmo: Linux 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64 GNU/Linux. Kernel identity alone proves no active containment.

MCP and resume evidence
No initialize/tools/list/lane_start exchange from an actual selected conductor client was available. The current tool metadata search exposed no lane_start/lane_brief endpoint. Repository lane_mcp.py implements those server-side surfaces, but server code, configuration entries and standalone queries cannot prove client attachment. The supplied lane_brief({}) Invalid params observation remains a connection/schema mismatch to diagnose, not evidence of server absence. Launch and resume each need trusted client/server transport correlation, catalogue/config/anchor checks and automatic bounded lane_start onboarding before control is handed over.

Smallest contract-preserving path
First resolve one complete enforcement mechanism for the requested Codex target before building three adapters. Use its installed native hook surface as the first candidate; independently prove actual tool names, nested-call/MCP coverage, missing/crashed/timed-out/malformed gate refusal, and successful canonical delegation without prompts. If native hooks cannot provide that boundary, a separately contracted trusted host mediation path must prove complete mediation while transferring work to the existing executor. App-server/ACP availability alone does not establish it. Grok requires such an alternative or a verified runtime correction; merely moving its hook into the SDK is insufficient.
Then complete the existing shared owners: task declarations/semantic acceptance, canonical dispatch execution and exact C2 output mechanisms, lane_policy evaluation and all acceptance transitions, followed by thin conduct startup. Explicit path checks found conduct, conduct.py, adapters.py, lane_policy.py and task/outputs.py absent; jobs.json contains zero outputs declarations. Existing probe.py measures configuration isolation, not the required conduct observation families.
The first usable tranche must successfully onboard, perform permitted reads/coordination, dispatch an admitted worker through the canonical service, return its accepted result, refuse forbidden operations before effects, and resume with unchanged authority plus a reverified MCP connection. A read-only shell that cannot dispatch, a prompt promising compliance, or a launcher that only refuses is not that tranche. Independent disposable live controls and verified mocks remain necessary before admission; none was run here.

No model launches, network requests, credential/store inspection, global configuration changes, edits, admission or PLAN.md creation occurred. Suites were not run because this assignment forbids writes. Codex informational commands reported failed PATH-alias creation attempts rejected by the read-only filesystem; no successful alias write was observed.
